questions.question: A booster pump can be used for filling as well as for emptying a tank. The capacity of the tank is 1800 m³. The emptying capacity of the tank is 10 m³/min higher than its filling capacity, and the pump needs 6 minutes lesser to empty the tank than it needs to fill it. What is the filling capacity of the pump in m³/min?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__
Let **filling capacity** be x. Then **emptying capacity** is x + 10.

Time difference formula: [Capacity / (Smaller Rate)] − [Capacity / (Larger Rate)] = Time Difference

1800/x − 1800/(x + 10) = 6

Test Option (3): x = 50 ⇒ 1800/50 − 1800/60 = 36 − 30 = 6 minutes. Matches exactly.

**∴ The correct answer is 50 m³/min.**

**__Alternate Method__**
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/873b037846b0acb706861f41d7c3360c250ac27e99926814a53490e88414dabc.png] 
**Given:** Total Tank Capacity = **1800 m³**, Difference in capacity = **10 m³/min**, Difference in time = **6 minutes**.

**Formula Used:** Time = Capacity ÷ Rate

⇒ Let Filling Capacity = x m³/min

⇒ Emptying Capacity = (x + 10) m³/min

⇒ 1800/x − 1800/(x + 10) = 6

⇒ 1800 [(x + 10 − x) / (x(x + 10))] = 6

⇒ 1800 × 10 / (x² + 10x) = 6

⇒ 3000 = x² + 10x

⇒ x² + 10x − 3000 = 0

⇒ (x + 60)(x − 50) = 0

⇒ Since capacity cannot be negative, x = 50 m³/min.

**∴ The correct answer is 50 m³/min.**

**__Additional Information__**

Time and Work Relation

Rate of work is inversely proportional to the time taken. If capacity increases, time decreases: Time = Work / Rate.

Quadratic Shortcut

For the equation x² + (a−b)x − ab = 0, the roots are b and −a. In physical problems like capacity, always pick the positive root.

Pipes and Cisterns

Filling is considered positive work while emptying is considered negative work in net efficiency problems.</p

questions.question: Which of the following soils is most suitable for rice cultivation in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alluvial soil**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alluvial soil** is the most suitable soil for rice cultivation due to its **fertility and moisture retention capacity**.
 
• It is rich in essential nutrients such as **potash, phosphoric acid, and lime**, which are required for the growth of rice plants.
 
• Alluvial soils are formed by the deposition of sediments brought by rivers such as the **Ganga, Brahmaputra, and Indus**.
 
• This soil type is widely found in the **Indo-Gangetic plain**, which is a major rice-growing region in India.
 
• It has a **clayey texture** that helps retain water, a crucial factor for rice cultivation as rice requires standing water during its growth phase.
 
• Alluvial soil is found in **low-lying areas** that are naturally irrigated by river systems, making it ideal for rice farming.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Desert Soil**__

 __
 
• **Desert soil** is found in arid regions such as **Rajasthan** and is characterized by low fertility and high sand content.
 
• It lacks moisture and organic content, making it unsuitable for rice cultivation.
 
• This soil type is typically used for crops that require minimal water, such as **millets and pulses**.
 
 
 
• **Red Soil**__
 __
 
• **Red soil** is found in regions such as **Chhattisgarh, Tamil Nadu, and Karnataka**.
 
• It is formed by the weathering of crystalline rocks and is rich in **iron oxide**, giving it a reddish color.
 
• Although it is fertile for crops like **groundnut, cotton, and millets**, it lacks essential nutrients such as nitrogen and organic matter, making it less suitable for rice cultivation.
 
 
 
• **Saline Soil**__
 
 
• **Saline soil** is characterized by high salt content and is found in areas such as **Rann of Kutch in Gujarat and coastal regions**.
 
• It is not suitable for most crops, including rice, due to its **poor drainage and high salinity**.
 
• Efforts are often required to reclaim saline soils for agricultural use.

questions.question: Find the greatest number by which when the numbers 247 and 189 are divided, it leaves remainders 3 and 6, respectively.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Subtract the remainders from the given numbers first:

247 − 3 = 244

189 − 6 = 183

Required number = HCF(244, 183)

Difference between 244 and 183 = 244 − 183 = 61

Since 61 is prime and divides both 244 (61 × 4) and 183 (61 × 3).

**∴ The correct answer is 61.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Numbers are 247 and 189.

Remainders are 3 and 6 respectively.

**Formula Used:**

The greatest number that divides A and B leaving remainders x and y is the HCF of (A − x) and (B − y).

questions.question: The length and breadth of a cuboid are 70 cm and 96 cm, respectively. If its surface area is 25392 cm², then what is the length (in cm) of its diagonal?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Surface Area = 2(lb + bh + hl)

25392 = 2(70 × 96 + 96h + 70h)

12696 = 6720 + 166h ⇒ 166h = 5976 ⇒ h = 36 cm

Diagonal = √(l² + b² + h²) = √(70² + 96² + 36²)

Diagonal = √(4900 + 9216 + 1296) = √15412 cm

**∴ The correct answer is √15412 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Length (l)** = 70 cm, **Breadth (b)** = 96 cm, **Total Surface Area** = 25392 cm².

**Formula Used:** Total Surface Area of Cuboid = 2(lb + bh + hl); Diagonal = √(l² + b² + h²)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/eee37f9023394f2ac20e27324f91040c4dd2520b184d38494bb3a3bb30200dcd.png] 

⇒ 2(70 × 96 + 96 × h + 70 × h) = 25392

⇒ 6720 + 166h = 12696

⇒ 166h = 12696 − 6720

⇒ 166h = 5976 ⇒ h = 36 cm

⇒ Diagonal (d) = √(70² + 96² + 36²)

⇒ d = √(4900 + 9216 + 1296)

⇒ d = √15412 cm

**∴ The correct answer is √15412 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of Cuboid

The space occupied by a cuboid is given by V = l × b × h.

Lateral Surface Area

The area of the four side walls is calculated as 2h(l + b).

Cube Properties

If l = b = h = a, the diagonal of a cube is √3 × a and the surface area is 6a².</p

questions.question: The sum of the perimeter of two cubes, the length of whose edges are x cm and y cm, respectively, is 300 cm and the product of edges x and y is 156 cm². Find the sum of the volume of both cubes.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Sum of **perimeters** of two **cubes** = 12(x + y) = 300 → x + y = 25 cm.

Given **product of edges** (xy) = 156 cm².

Sum of **volumes** = x³ + y³ = (x + y)((x + y)² − 3xy).

x³ + y³ = 25 × (25² − 3 × 156) = 25 × (625 − 468) = 25 × 157 = 3925 cm³.

**∴ The correct answer is 3925 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Total perimeter = 300 cm, Product of edges (xy) = 156 cm².

**Formula:** Perimeter of a cube = 12 × edge; Volume = edge³.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b2ed1338349249a950c6c01d691989456c29e01a834ca7834b1c05f3046ac433.png] 

⇒ 12x + 12y = 300

⇒ 12(x + y) = 300 ⇒ x + y = 25

⇒ Sum of volumes = x³ + y³

⇒ x³ + y³ = (x + y)³ − 3xy(x + y)

⇒ x³ + y³ = (25)³ − 3(156)(25)

⇒ x³ + y³ = 15625 − 11700

⇒ x³ + y³ = 3925 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 3925 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cube Properties

Total surface area of a cube is 6a² and the longest diagonal is a√3, where a is the edge length.

Algebraic Identity

The sum of cubes formula: a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²) or (a + b)³ − 3ab(a + b).

Perimeter of 3D shapes

The total edge length (perimeter) of a cube/cuboid is the sum of all 12 edges.</p

questions.question: An article is sold for x. If it is sold at 40% of this price, there is a loss of 50%. What is the percentage profit when it is sold for ₹x?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **selling price** x = 100.

New Selling Price = 40% of 100 = 40.

Loss is 50%, so **Cost Price** (CP) = 40 ÷ (1 − 0.50) = 80.

Profit at price x = 100 − 80 = 20.

Profit % = (20 ÷ 80) × 100 = 25%.

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: SP₁ = x | SP₂ = 0.40x | Loss% = 50%
Formulas: CP = SP × 100 ÷ (100 − Loss%) | Profit% = (SP − CP) ÷ CP × 100
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2c5735d8cfd50e3573d8c6cc601a8129721eb03b6bffe3c8e7b2634778b25939.png] 
⇒ When sold at 0.40x, Loss = 50%, so CP = 0.40x ÷ 0.50 = 0.80x.
⇒ To find profit when sold at x: Profit = x − 0.80x = 0.20x.
⇒ Profit % = (0.20x ÷ 0.80x) × 100 = (1 ÷ 4) × 100 = 25%.

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Selling Price and Cost Price Relationship

If an object is sold at a **loss**, the CP is always greater than the SP. Formula: CP = SP + Loss.

Profit Percentage

Profit percentage is always calculated on the **Cost Price** unless stated otherwise. Formula: (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.</p

questions.question: Reena, Naveen and Arpita started a business in partnership, investing in the ratio of 5 : 6 :13, respectively. At the end of the year, they earned a profit of ₹36,400, which is 14% of their total investment. How much did Naveen invest (in ₹)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total **ratio parts** of investment = 5 + 6 + 13 = 24 units.

Given **Total Profit** = ₹36,400, which is 14% of the investment.

Total **Investment** = (36,400 ÷ 14) × 100 = ₹2,60,000.

**Naveen's share** in investment = (6 ÷ 24) × 2,60,000.

Naveen's investment = 1/4 × 2,60,000 = ₹65,000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹65,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Ratio = 5 : 6 : 13 | Profit = ₹36,400 | Profit % = 14%.
Formulas: Total Investment = (Profit ÷ Profit%) × 100 | Individual Share = (Individual Ratio ÷ Total Ratio) × Total Investment.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d0d2bb7a666d09e4f0e6af94845400bd210fa299bc2f8e12a79e61ab77528078.png] 
⇒ Calculate **Total Investment**: 14% = 36,400
⇒ 100% = (36,400 × 100) ÷ 14 = 2,600 × 100 = 2,60,000
⇒ Sum of ratio components = 5 + 6 + 13 = 24
⇒ **Naveen's Investment** = (6 ÷ 24) × 2,60,000
⇒ Naveen's Investment = (1 ÷ 4) × 2,60,000 = 65,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹65,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Partnership Investment

In a partnership, if the time period is constant, the profit is distributed in the same ratio as the **capital investment**.

Percentage to Absolute Value

To find the base value (Total Investment) from a percentage: Base = (Value ÷ Percentage) × 100.

questions.question: What is the unit of measurement for frequenсу?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Hertz (Hz)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Hertz (Hz)** is the **SI unit of frequency**, which measures the number of cycles of a periodic wave per second.
 
• It is named after the German physicist **Heinrich Rudolf Hertz**, who made significant contributions to the understanding of electromagnetic waves.
 
• 1 Hertz represents **one cycle per second**. For example, a frequency of 50 Hz means there are 50 cycles of the wave occurring each second.
 
• The unit is widely used in various fields such as **physics, telecommunications, acoustics, and electronics** to describe the frequency of waves, including sound waves, electromagnetic waves, and alternating current.
 
• Applications of frequency measurement in **Hertz** include **radio broadcasting** (e.g., FM radio operates at 88-108 MHz), **electricity** (standard power supply frequency is 50 Hz or 60 Hz), and **digital systems** (e.g., processor clock speeds in GHz).
 
• The **Hertz** is a derived unit, and its dimensional formula is **T⁻¹**, where T represents time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Millisecond**__

 __
 
• A **millisecond** (ms) is a unit of time and is equal to **one-thousandth of a second** (1 ms = 0.001 seconds).
 
• It is commonly used in fields like **computer science** and **electronics** to measure short time intervals, such as **response times**.
 
 
 
• **Pascal**__
 __
 
• The **Pascal (Pa)** is the SI unit of **pressure**, not frequency.
 
• It is defined as **one newton per square meter** (1 Pa = 1 N/m²).
 
• This unit is used to measure pressure in various fields such as **fluid dynamics, meteorology, and material science**.
 
 
 
• **Joule**__
 
 
• The **Joule (J)** is the SI unit of **energy**, not frequency.
 
• It is defined as the **work done** when a force of one newton moves an object one meter (1 J = 1 N·m).
 
• It is used in fields like **physics, engineering, and thermodynamics** to measure energy, work, or heat.

questions.question: Kavita buys 2 apples and 5 mangoes for ₹239. When the cost of an apple is decreased by 50% and that of a mango remains the same, then the cost of 2 apples and 4 mangoes is ₹184. What is the original cost of 8 apples and 8 mangoes?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the cost of an **apple** be A and a **mango** be M.

From the given data: 2A + 5M = 239 and A + 4M = 184 (since 50% of 2A = A).

Multiply the second equation by 2: 2A + 8M = 368.

Difference: 3M = 368 − 239 = 129 ⇒ M = 43.

Then A = 184 − 4(43) = 12. Sum of 1A + 1M = 12 + 43 = 55.

Required cost for 8 apples and 8 mangoes = 8 × 55 = 440.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹440.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial condition: 2 **apples** + 5 **mangoes** = ₹239

Condition after 50% decrease in apple price: 2(0.5 × apple) + 4 **mangoes** = ₹184

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f41a854c654938435110cdb94cbfd8b8f51956f1cfce32220fce0100e60dcf24.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let A be the original cost of an **apple** and M be the cost of a **mango**.

⇒ 2A + 5M = 239 --- (Equation 1)

⇒ 2(A − 50% of A) + 4M = 184

⇒ 2(0.5A) + 4M = 184 ⇒ A + 4M = 184 --- (Equation 2)

From Eq 2, we get A = 184 − 4M. Substituting this in Eq 1:

⇒ 2(184 − 4M) + 5M = 239

⇒ 368 − 8M + 5M = 239

⇒ 368 − 3M = 239

⇒ 3M = 368 − 239 = 129 ⇒ M = ₹43

Substitute M = 43 in Eq 2:

⇒ A = 184 − 4(43) = 184 − 172 = ₹12

Original cost of 8 **apples** and 8 **mangoes**:

⇒ 8A + 8M = 8(12) + 8(43)

⇒ 96 + 344 = 440

**∴ The correct answer is ₹440.**

When an object is **recast**, its **volume remains constant**.

For a cone, Volume ∝ r²h.

⇒ r₁²h₁ = r₂²h₂

⇒ (17.6)² × 6.7 = (8.8)² × h₂

⇒ (2 × 8.8)² × 6.7 = (8.8)² × h₂ ⇒ 4 × 6.7 = h₂ = 26.8 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 26.8 cm.**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Volume of old cone = Volume of new cone

⇒ (1/3) × π × (r₁)² × h₁ = (1/3) × π × (r₂)² × h₂

⇒ (r₁)² × h₁ = (r₂)² × h₂

⇒ (17.6)² × 6.7 = (8.8)² × h₂

⇒ h₂ = (17.6 × 17.6 × 6.7) / (8.8 × 8.8)

⇒ h₂ = 2 × 2 × 6.7

⇒ h₂ = 4 × 6.7 = 26.8 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 26.8 cm.**

The Correct answer is __**1835**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The formal introduction of **English education** in India by the British took place in the year **1835**.
 
• This decision was largely influenced by the ideas of **Thomas Babington Macaulay**, who advocated for the promotion of English education in his famous **Minute on Education**.
 
• Macaulay argued that English education would create a class of Indians who were **"Indian in blood and color, but English in taste, opinions, morals, and intellect."**
 
• The **Charter Act of 1813** had earlier allowed for the allocation of funds to promote education in India, but it was in **1835** that the focus shifted explicitly to English education.
 
• As a result of this shift, the British introduced English as the medium of instruction in schools and colleges, particularly in higher education.
 
• Institutions such as the **Calcutta Medical College** (established in 1835) began using English as the primary medium of teaching.
 
• This marked the beginning of a significant cultural and educational transformation in India, with English becoming a key language for administration, education, and intellectual discourse.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **1813**__

 __
 
• The **Charter Act of 1813** marked the first step by the British to involve themselves in the promotion of education in India.
 
• It allocated a sum of **1 lakh rupees annually** for the "revival and promotion of literature" and the introduction of "useful knowledge" in India.
 
• However, no specific emphasis on English education was made under this act.
 
 
 
• **1854**__
 __
 
• The year **1854** is significant for the **Wood's Despatch**, which laid the foundation for the modern education system in India.
 
• It recommended the establishment of **universities in Bombay, Calcutta, and Madras** and proposed a system of education at all levels (primary, secondary, and higher).
 
• The despatch also emphasized the use of both English and vernacular languages in education.
 
 
 
• **1829**__
 
 
• The year **1829** is historically significant for the abolition of **Sati** under the efforts of **Raja Ram Mohan Roy** and Governor-General **Lord William Bentinck**.
 
• It does not directly relate to the introduction of English education in India.

questions.question: If 600 bananas were distributed among three monkeys in the ratio (1)/(14) : (1)/(2) : (9)/(3) respectively, how many bananas did the third monkey get?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Convert fractional ratio to whole numbers by multiplying by **LCM** of denominators (14, 2, 1) = 14.

New Ratio → (1/14 × 14) : (1/2 × 14) : (3 × 14) = 1 : 7 : 42.

Total units = 1 + 7 + 42 = 50 units. Given 50 units = 600 bananas ⇒ 1 unit = 12.

Third monkey = 42 units × 12 = 504.

**∴ The correct answer is 504 bananas.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8b89b199864af33829662458ba8d410db850cff6bd2c365162e9ddace4555b81.png] 

**Given:** Total bananas = 600. Ratio = 1/14 : 1/2 : 3.

**Formula:** Value of share = (Specific Ratio / Sum of Ratios) × Total Value.

⇒ Simplified Ratio = (1/14 × 14) : (1/2 × 14) : (3 × 14)

⇒ Simplified Ratio = 1 : 7 : 42

⇒ Sum of ratio parts = 1 + 7 + 42 = 50

⇒ Share of **Third Monkey** = (42 / 50) × 600

⇒ Share of **Third Monkey** = 42 × 12 = 504

**∴ The correct answer is 504 bananas.**

**__Additional Information__**

Compound Ratio

The compound ratio of two ratios a:b and c:d is (a×c) : (b×d).

Invertendo and Alternendo

If a:b = c:d, then b:a = d:c (Invertendo) and a:c = b:d (Alternendo).

Ratio Normalization

To convert a fractional ratio to a whole number ratio, multiply all terms by the **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** of all denominators.</p

questions.question: The coordination number of atoms in a body-centered cubic (BCC) lattice is:
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**8**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **coordination number** refers to the number of nearest neighbor atoms surrounding a particular atom in a crystal lattice.
 
• In a **body-centered cubic (BCC)** lattice, each atom is surrounded by **8 nearest neighbors**.
 
• The BCC structure consists of atoms located at the **corners of the cube** and one atom at the **center of the cube**.
 
• Each corner atom is shared among **8 adjacent unit cells**, while the central atom belongs entirely to the unit cell.
 
• The coordination number of 8 arises from the geometry of the lattice, where the central atom is equidistant from the 8 corner atoms.
 
• This arrangement is commonly found in metals like **iron, chromium, and tungsten**, which adopt the BCC structure.
 
• The BCC lattice is less densely packed compared to other structures like **face-centered cubic (FCC)** or **hexagonal close-packed (HCP)**, but it provides good mechanical stability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **6**__

 __
 
• A coordination number of **6** is typically observed in structures like the **simple cubic lattice**.
 
• In the simple cubic lattice, each atom is surrounded by **6 nearest neighbors**, positioned along the faces of the cube.
 
• This structure is relatively rare in nature due to its low packing efficiency.
 
 
 
• **4**__
 __
 
• A coordination number of **4** is common in structures like **diamond cubic lattices**, where atoms form tetrahedral bonds.
 
• It is observed in materials like **silicon** and **diamond**, which exhibit strong covalent bonding.
 
 
 
• **12**__
 
 
• A coordination number of **12** is observed in densely packed structures like **face-centered cubic (FCC)** and **hexagonal close-packed (HCP)** lattices.
 
• These structures are highly efficient in packing and are commonly found in metals like **gold, aluminum, and copper**.
 
• The high coordination number contributes to their exceptional mechanical and thermal properties.

questions.question: At what rate (in percentage) per annum simple interest will a sum of money triple itself in 8 years?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For a sum of money to become **n times** of itself at **Simple Interest**, the formula for **Rate (R)** is:

**Rate (R) = [(n − 1) ÷ Time (T)] × 100**

Given: **n = 3** (sum triples) and **T = 8 years**.

⇒ R = [(3 − 1) ÷ 8] × 100 = (2 ÷ 8) × 100 = (1 ÷ 4) × 100 = 25%.

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Let the **Principal (P)** = ₹100

The sum **triples** itself, so **Amount (A)** = 3 × 100 = ₹300

**Time (T)** = 8 years

**Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100**

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI = Amount − Principal = 300 − 100 = ₹200

⇒ 200 = (100 × R × 8) ÷ 100

⇒ 200 = R × 8

⇒ R = 200 ÷ 8

⇒ R = 25%

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

__
 
• **Relative Reference** in MS Excel adjusts both the **column letter** and **row number** automatically when a formula is copied to another location.
 
• This type of reference is extremely useful when creating formulas that need to be applied across multiple rows or columns dynamically.
 
• For example, if you use a formula like **=A1+B1** in a cell and copy it to another location, the formula will automatically adjust to **=A2+B2**, **=A3+B3**, and so on.
 
• **Relative references** are the default reference type in MS Excel unless explicitly changed.
 
• They save time and effort by eliminating the need to manually rewrite formulas for different cells.
 
• Relative references are denoted without any **$** symbols, e.g., **A1**.
 
• This type of reference is widely used in scenarios such as **data analysis, calculations, and creating dynamic tables**.

• Absolute references use **$** symbols to lock both the column and row, e.g., **$A$1**.
 
 
 
• **Mixed Reference**__

• **Mixed references** in MS Excel lock either the **column** or the **row**, but not both.
 
• Examples of mixed references include **$A1** (column locked) or **A$1** (row locked).
 
• This type of reference is useful for creating formulas where partial adjustments are needed during copying.
 
 
 
• **Absolute Reference**__
 
 
• An **absolute reference** in MS Excel locks both the **row** and **column**, ensuring that the reference remains constant, no matter where the formula is copied.

questions.question: The average of five numbers is 56. Four of the numbers are 35, 42, 32, and 26. What is the fifth number?

Assume the base **average** is 56.

Calculate **deviations** of given numbers: (35−56) + (42−56) + (32−56) + (26−56)

**Given:** Average of **5 numbers** = 56. Known numbers = **35, 42, 32, 26**.

⇒ x = 145

questions.question: The successive discounts of 24%, 18% and 20% are equivalent to a single discount of: (Rounded up to two decimal places.)

= 57.68 − 7.536 = 50.144%.

questions.question: If the median of a data is 20.8 less than its mode, then the median of the data exceeds its mean by _____. (Use the empirical formula)
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Using the empirical relationship: **Mode − Median = 2 × (Median − Mean)**

Given: **Mode − Median = 20.8**

⇒ 2 × (Median − Mean) = 20.8

⇒ Median − Mean = 20.8 ÷ 2 = 10.4

**∴ The correct answer is 10.4.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The median of the data is 20.8 less than its mode.

⇒ Median = Mode − 20.8

⇒ Mode − Median = 20.8

**Formula Used:**

The empirical relationship between Mean, Median, and Mode is:

**Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/455795f3bb2df1f7a9c28e28eb3a86653c0cf11079f1806c54522051c33c0100.png] 

**Calculations:**

Subtracting Median from both sides of the empirical formula:

⇒ Mode − Median = (3 × Median − 2 × Mean) − Median

⇒ Mode − Median = 2 × Median − 2 × Mean

⇒ Mode − Median = 2 × (Median − Mean)

Substitute the given value of (Mode − Median = 20.8):

⇒ 20.8 = 2 × (Median − Mean)

⇒ Median − Mean = 20.8 ÷ 2

⇒ Median − Mean = 10.4

Thus, the median of the data exceeds its mean by 10.4.

**Why other options are incorrect:**

Empirical Formula

questions.question: One-third of a journey is covered at a speed of 67 km/hr, the next one-third of the journey is covered at a speed of 66 km/hr, and the remaining journey is covered at a speed of 17 km/hr. The average speed (in km/hr, rounded off to one decimal place) for the entire journey is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__
When equal distances are covered at speeds **s₁**, **s₂**, and **s₃**, the **Average Speed** = 3 × s₁ × s₂ × s₃ ÷ (s₁s₂ + s₂s₃ + s₃s₁).

Average Speed = (3 × 67 × 66 × 17) ÷ (67 × 66 + 66 × 17 + 17 × 67)

Average Speed = 225522 ÷ (4422 + 1122 + 1139) = 225522 ÷ 6683 ≈ 33.745 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 33.7 kmph.**

**__Alternate Method__**
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/eb7337969f55ad6080f0321dbc5fa5b126bda1ee339b0180ee395099a2192a1b.png] 
**Given:** Speeds s₁ = 67 km/hr, s₂ = 66 km/hr, s₃ = 17 km/hr. Each covers 1/3rd distance.

**Formula Used:** Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

⇒ Let total distance be 3 units. Then each part is 1 unit.

⇒ Total Time = (1 ÷ 67) + (1 ÷ 66) + (1 ÷ 17)

⇒ Total Time = (66 × 17 + 67 × 17 + 67 × 66) ÷ (67 × 66 × 17)

⇒ Total Time = (1122 + 1139 + 4422) ÷ 75174 = 6683 ÷ 75174

⇒ Average Speed = 3 ÷ (6683 ÷ 75174)

⇒ Average Speed = (3 × 75174) ÷ 6683 = 225522 ÷ 6683

⇒ Average Speed ≈ 33.745 km/hr ≈ 33.7 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 33.7 kmph.**

**__Additional Information__**

Average Speed Formula

For two equal distances covered at speeds a and b, Average Speed = 2ab ÷ (a + b).

Relative Speed

Objects moving in same direction: Relative speed = S₁ − S₂. In opposite direction: Relative speed = S₁ + S₂.

Rounding Rules

If the digit to be dropped is 5 or more, increase the preceding digit by 1 (e.g., 33.745 becomes 33.7 if rounding to 1st decimal).</p

questions.question: There are two sections A and B of a class, consisting of 22 and 44 students, respectively. If the average weight of section A is 40 kg and that of section B is 37 kg, find the average weight of the whole class (in kg).
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **students** in Section A to Section B = 22 : 44 = 1 : 2.

Weight of **Section A** is 40 kg and **Section B** is 37 kg.

Assume 37 kg as **base weight**; Deviation for Section A = 40 − 37 = +3 kg.

Net deviation distributed over total ratio parts = (1 × 3) ÷ (1 + 2) = 3 ÷ 3 = 1 kg.

Required **Average Weight** = 37 + 1 = 38 kg.

**∴ The correct answer is 38 kg.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of students in **Section A** (n₁) = 22

Average weight of **Section A** (w₁) = 40 kg

Number of students in **Section B** (n₂) = 44

Average weight of **Section B** (w₂) = 37 kg

**Formula Used:**

Combined Average = (n₁w₁ + n₂w₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7d451ee0fd5ca45716a334f7625181417c80df3e566e8c2026e99bc019acb55e.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total weight of **Section A** = 22 × 40 = 880 kg

⇒ Total weight of **Section B** = 44 × 37 = 1628 kg

⇒ Total weight of the whole **class** = 880 + 1628 = 2508 kg

⇒ Total number of **students** = 22 + 44 = 66

⇒ Average weight of the **class** = 2508 ÷ 66

⇒ Average weight = 38 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 38 kg.**

**__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Principle

When two groups are combined, the resulting average always lies between the averages of the individual groups. It is closer to the average of the group with more members.

Ratio Method for Averages

Instead of using actual student counts, the **ratio of quantities** can be used in the formula: Average = (R₁A₁ + R₂A₂) ÷ (R₁ + R₂), where R represents the ratio parts.

Deviation Concept

Net Deviation = Sum of (Value − Assumed Average). For the final average, the net deviation must be zero across all items.</p

⇒ Option 2: **1440** → (1 + 4) − (4 + 0) = 5 − 4 = 1 (Not divisible)

⇒ Option 3: **2118** → (2 + 1) − (1 + 8) = 3 − 9 = −6 (Not divisible)

Divisibility by 3

A number is divisible by 3 if the **sum of its digits** is divisible by 3.

Divisibility by 9

A number is divisible by 9 if the **sum of its digits** is divisible by 9.

Divisibility by 4

A number is divisible by 4 if the **last two digits** are divisible by 4.</p

questions.question: Which prominent Indian leader led the Bardoli Satyagraha of 1928, a major civil disobedience movement against increased land taxes?

• The movement was successful in forcing the British government to **roll back the increased revenue**, making it a landmark victory for civil disobedience.
 
• For his leadership in Bardoli, Vallabhbhai Patel earned the title of **Sardar**, which means ‘leader’ or ‘chief’.

questions.question: Anand purchased an item and incurred ₹169 in repair expenses. Subsequently, he sold it to Bharath with a 25% profit. Eventually, Bharath sold the item for ₹4,480, making a 44% loss. What was the original cost (in₹) of the item for Anand?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Successive multiplier: Total SP = (Original Cost + Repair) × 1.25 × 0.56.

Given final SP = 4,480.

Bharath's CP = 4,480 ÷ 0.56 = 8,000.

Anand's Total CP = 8,000 ÷ 1.25 = 6,400.

Original Cost = 6,400 − 169 = 6,231.

**∴ The correct answer is 6,231.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Formulas: Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 | Loss% = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100 | SP = CP × (100 ± P/L)% ÷ 100
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/38ab7a3f7d72349daeed60be47a07181c939fc28f45049df3f4f7c61cd313920.png] 

⇒ Let the **Original Cost** of the item be x.

⇒ Anand's **Total Cost Price** = (x + 169).

⇒ **Selling Price** to Bharath = (x + 169) × (125 ÷ 100) = 1.25(x + 169).

⇒ Bharath's **Selling Price** = 1.25(x + 169) × (100 − 44) ÷ 100 = 4,480.

⇒ 1.25(x + 169) × 0.56 = 4,480.

⇒ 0.7(x + 169) = 4,480.

⇒ x + 169 = 4,480 ÷ 0.7 = 6,400.

⇒ x = 6,400 − 169 = 6,231.

**∴ The correct answer is 6,231.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Cost Price

The **Effective Cost Price** includes the purchase price plus any overhead expenses like **repairs**, transport, or labor. Formula: Total CP = Purchase Price + Overheads.

Chain Rules in Profit & Loss

In a chain of transactions, the **Selling Price** for the first person becomes the **Cost Price** for the second person.</p

⇒ Population in 1976 = 2,07,300 × 1.2 × 1.2

⇒ Population in 1976 = 2,07,300 × 1.44

⇒ Population in 1976 = 298512

**∴ The correct answer is 2,98,512.**

Successive Percentage Change

If a value changes by a% and then by b%, the net percentage change is given by (a + b + ab/100)%.

Population Depreciation

If the population decreases at a constant rate r, the future population is calculated as P × (1 − r/100)ⁿ.

Compounding Frequency

Population growth follows the same mathematical principle as compound interest where growth is added to the updated base each period.</p

questions.question: A woman travelled at a speed of 20 m/min for 80 min, and at a speed of 65 m/min for 70 min. Her average speed (in m/min) is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__
**Weighted Average** of speed = (v₁t₁ + v₂t₂) ÷ (t₁ + t₂)

Ratio of **time** = 80 : 70 = 8 : 7

Average speed = [(20 × 8) + (65 × 7)] ÷ (8 + 7)

Average speed = (160 + 455) ÷ 15 = 615 ÷ 15 = 41 m/min

**∴ The correct answer is 41 m/min.**

**__Alternate Method__**
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0d2adf38b3eaea55a9d99efb29a90fb87b311f212fa15b250ab632739811ce6c.png] 
**Given:**

Speed 1 (v₁) = 20 m/min, Time 1 (t₁) = 80 min

Speed 2 (v₂) = 65 m/min, Time 2 (t₂) = 70 min

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = **Total Distance** ÷ **Total Time**

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = (20 × 80) + (65 × 70)

⇒ Total Distance = 1600 + 4550 = 6150 meters

⇒ Total Time = 80 + 70 = 150 min

⇒ Average Speed = 6150 ÷ 150

⇒ Average Speed = 41 m/min

**∴ The correct answer is 41 m/min.**

**__Additional Information__**

Average Speed (Equal Distances)

When two equal distances are covered at speeds u and v, average speed = 2uv ÷ (u + v).

Relative Speed

Objects moving in the same direction: Relative Speed = |u − v|. Opposite direction: Relative Speed = u + v.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.</p
